title: 🏛️ Exams 2008–2021 · will and if in exam texts ⭐⭐

questions.prompt: (Exam 2018, general) A young adult looks back at his school days and warns his readers. Which form completes the end of the sentence? "…because if you don't, then you ___ it."
questions.explanation: The clause "if you don't" states a condition, and what follows is its result, a prediction told with will + base verb: will regret. "are regretting" is a present continuous and "regretted" is a past form, so neither tells a result to come; "will regrets" adds an -s after will.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2018, general) A young adult writes: "I advise everyone to cherish those days because if you don't, then…" What does "if you don't" mean here?

options.text: if you don't give this advice to everyone
if you don't spend your first day at school
if you don't tell anybody about those days
if you don't cherish those days

questions.explanation: In "if you don't", the short form don't stands for the verb of the advice, which is not repeated: the condition is "if you don't cherish those days". The result comes after "then". The other readings give the condition a verb that the sentence does not use before "because".

questions.prompt: (Exam 2012, general) Tony, a 15-year-old school boy, belongs to an environmental organization. His group starts a new tree-planting project next month. Which form completes the sentence? "Tony hopes many people ___ him in such a project to protect the earth."
questions.explanation: The project has not started yet, so Tony hopes for something to come: will + base verb, will join. "joined" is a finished action; "joins" does not agree with the plural "many people"; "will joins" adds an -s after will.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2008) A mother tells how her son asked her to stop smoking: "Mum, don't smoke. You ___ of cancer."
questions.explanation: The child warns his mother about the result of smoking, a prediction told with will + base verb: will die. "are dying" describes something that is happening now; "will dies" adds an -s after will; "must die" is a modal with another meaning than a prediction of a result.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2021, general) A text about online shopping lists its drawbacks. Which word completes the sentence? "Besides, ___ e-commerce sites are not secure, your personal data is at risk of falling into the wrong hands."
questions.explanation: "if" opens the condition: when the sites are not secure, the data is at risk. "unless" means "if not": "unless the sites are not secure" would say that the data is at risk when the sites are secure, which makes no sense; "like" and "never" cannot open the clause.

questions.prompt: (Exam 2008) In a text, a boy says to his mother: "Mum, don't smoke. You must die of cancer." What does must express in this sentence?

options.text: A possibility: you may die of cancer
An obligation: you have to die of cancer
A permission: you are allowed to die of cancer
An ability: you are able to die of cancer

questions.explanation: Must expresses an obligation (you have to). Said to a mother who smokes, "You must die of cancer" would order her to die, which is not what the boy means, so the sentence does not warn her about a result. Possibility is told with may, might or could, not with must; permission and ability belong to other modals.
